newsitem.title: USA: Semiconductor revenues to drop - Study.
newsitem.headline: Semiconductor revenues to drop - Study.

text.p: Semiconductor revenues are expected to drop more than 9 percent to $137 billion worldwide this year, according to a revised study released Tuesday by technology market research firm Dataquest.
An earlier forecast predicted a drop of 7.6 percent.
Dataquest attributed the revised forecast to a variety of factors, including heavy inventories and falling prices for dynamic random access memory chips, the memory chips in personal computers.

Memory chip prices have fallen by 80 percent in the last year. Thirty-two megabits worth of memory now sells for one-third less than an eight-megabit memory did a year ago but has four times the processing power, noted Robertson Stephens & Co. analyst Dan Klesken.
However, while the semiconductor market has taken a negative slide, Dataquest said the worst may be over.
With computer markets "firming up next year and an end to the memory price slide, we expect 1997 to be a growth year for the industry," Dataquest said.

In recent months, the semiconductor's key demand indicator -- the book-to-bill ratio of orders to shipments -- has shown improvement, leading analysts to predict the market is starting to rebound. Last month, the book-to-bill ratio hit 0.99, the highest level this year.

Dataquest said all of the major regions of the world will suffer large revenue declines this year, but Japan will see the largest decline in 1996 because the yen-to-dollar exchange rate continues to decline rapidly as compared to 1995.
